messages.text: A and I both want the trailer in the next few weeks, and neither of us is backing down. B's pad is where it lives, so she is stuck in the middle. Can you help the three of us sort this out?

1) I need to use it for my home project in the next few weeks, and I won’t just wait for A.  
2) I don’t see this as “neither of us backing down”; I want a workable way to use the trailer soon.  
3) Yes, I don’t want B made responsible for deciding between us.  
4) A is both my coworker and neighbor, so I want to keep this straightforward and not let it spill over.

Current list: no confirmed entries yet; please check whether that wording fits before adding anything.

It’s a little in my way, and I’d prefer it not stay on my pad long-term. I feel awkward saying that since I went along with the arrangement, and I don’t want to put pressure on either of you. I rent, so my landlord would need to approve any change to what’s kept there; I haven’t asked him. So that’s unresolved, not a decision. The list and pace are okay for now.

1. Fits: my project is soon, so its timing needs to count.  
2. Change to “being able to plan my own use, not simply wait for A.” I need room to manage my project schedule.  
3. Fits: I want my position represented accurately.  
4. Fits: B shouldn’t have to choose between us.  
5. Fits: keep this straightforward and contained. Nothing else I’m holding back.

My main concern is using the trailer for weekend trips in the next few weeks; my trips start soon, so I want this settled by then. I know C wants it soon too. I don’t have a concern about B’s pad, being asked to take sides, or working with C. The shared-list wording and pace are fine.

1–4 mostly fit: I want the space usable, not committed indefinitely, and to be able to revisit this without blame or pressure. 5: change to “understanding what my tenancy allows before anything changes”—I haven’t checked with my landlord. That matters because I don’t want to assume I can approve a change. I’m not sure I’m holding anything else back; the wording feels a little formal, but no major discomfort. Please don’t record these yet.

1, 3, 5, and 6 fit.  
2. Change to: “being able to plan and use the trailer for my project in the next few weeks, not simply wait for A.” I need to manage my own schedule.  
4. Change to: “having my own trailer use planned soon enough for my project.” The timing matters because I need it in the next few weeks.  
“Nothing else I’m holding back” still fits. No minor discomfort with the pace or list.

1–5 fit, and you can record them; please keep 5 unresolved. What matters is having usable space, not being committed indefinitely, and being able to revisit this without blame or pressure. I’m not sure because I don’t have anything specific else to add right now. 6 is a minor discomfort: plain wording helps, but it doesn’t need its own entry. The pace and list are okay.

1. Change to “being able to use the trailer for my weekend trips.”  
2. Fits: I want clarity before my trips start.  
3. Not sure that’s a concern for me; I just know C wants it soon too.  
4. I’m not concerned about those things, but that wording doesn’t fit as a concern. I’m not holding anything back about the work/neighbor overlap, and the pace and shared list are fine.

1, 3, 5, and 6 fit. 2 needs to say: “being able to plan and use the trailer for my project in the next few weeks, not simply wait for A.” 4 fits. The timing matters because my project needs the trailer soon; the rest matters because I want my position represented accurately and B not pressured. Nothing else I’m holding back, and no discomfort from me with the pace, list, B’s wording, or leaving #6 out. I can’t speak for A or B.

#2 fits: I need my timing taken seriously so I can plan my project, rather than just wait. #4 fits: I need dependable, timely planning for my project. “Nothing else I’m holding back” still fits; no discomfort from me with the other wording, pace, or list. I can’t speak for A or B.

1. “Having my own plans taken seriously” fits. I want room to make my own plans and use the trailer; that matters because my trips are coming up.  
2. Fits. I need clarity so I can plan before the trips start.  
3. No entry. C wanting it soon is information, not a concern for me.  
4. No entry. Those aren’t concerns.  
I expect my needs to matter equally. I’m not holding anything back, and the pace and shared list are fine.

Nothing else is held back. O1 doesn’t ensure my trailer use is planned soon; O2 is closest, but overlap remains unresolved. O3 doesn’t work for me as a pause—I need to use the trailer in the next few weeks, not simply wait. I can speak only for myself.

[16] Fits—I need dependable planning for use soon.  
[17] Fits—overlap needs addressing before windows are workable.  
[18] Fits—I need my timely use to remain active, not be set aside.  
Nothing else is held back; no discomfort from me. I can’t speak for A or B.
